title: Sir Gawain — Dialect and Spelling
subtitle: Northwest Midlands, not London.
objectives: Master Sir Gawain — Dialect and Spelling.
Read and translate authentic Middle English texts.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Northwest Midlands dialect, c. 1380–1400. Spelling differs from Chaucer: quen (when), quyl (while), schulde (should), -3 (yogh) for -gh or -y. Pronunciation differs slightly. The Gawain poet writes in a more conservative dialect than Chaucer.

items.prompt: What is the focus of this lesson?
Can you apply this to reading?
items.answer: Work through examples with your notes.
